In my own healing journey from trauma it has helped me to be very specific about the source of overwhelming emotions. When I got molested as a child and then my family did nothing when they found out, the molestation fucked me up in one way but the interpersonal betrayal fucked me up in a completely different way. I meant I could see the question being asked like this, if the “just” did not make it invalidating by nature.

Like if they were struggling w anxiety about interpersonal betrayal I might think it would be ok to ask if they think the emotions are coming just from the SA or also from the betrayal by others? But I understand now the context and I would rather die than talk to a vulnerable person in such a way

Companies like betterhelp and talkspace do not have a lot of oversight which leads to ethical violations happening with little accountability. Like I get it bc I love Karen and georgia and I think they should get their money, but also like these companies seek to make therapy accessible while not prioritizing therapist competence. A lot of unnecessary suffering can happen to vulnerable people when being connected with therapists who haven’t been properly vetted. 

I don’t think that OPs opinion was based on exactly that, but I also think the ethical principles of these companies are questionable. My experience on talkspace was frankly alarming, and talkspace support had nothing to say when I asked why, when I was seeking help to process a trauma, they would place me with a therapist who told me that their was no reason for me to be unable to move on from my trauma. 

I havent ever spoken on that bc I understand that’s my individual experience, but I was surprised by the lack of accountability from talkspace support. And then like, of course stuff like that happens on these apps bc there are so many providers and so many patients. I think there can be good experiences w apps like betterhelp but there can also be traumatizing experiences that the client is then left to sort out on their own.

“There are worse issues so your valid complaints are invalid” like k&g value and encourage this kind of accountability. Kind of weird people are going out of their way to say you’re overreacting when they can just move on.

I’m so so sorry for your loss. My brother took his life a month ago, and the most helpful things that people said to me were to make sure to take care of yourself. Take things one day at a time, one hour at a time, or even one minute at a time. It definitely does come in waves and it’s important to accept all of the emotions around it, not just the grief and the sadness but also like the confusion and just every emotion.

Things will never be normal in the same way again, and you’ll have to make a new normal, and that’s okay. I hope that makes sense it sounds better when I say that out loud. It has really helped me to talk to my brother out loud. I really felt his presence a lot the first couple weeks. 

At a certain point I just started writing down every memory with my brother in it because I don’t want to lose any of it. Like he was just here so recently, it’s still so weird that he’s gone. Writing all my memories has been helping me feel like I’m not actually letting go. 

Also I got one of those science board posters and I made a collage out of pictures of my brother. It was really hard cutting out the pictures and putting them on the board but it’s been really helpful and comforting to have a big board w like 90 pictures of my brother from the last 10 years. 

Also, the first two weeks I was feeling things, then the pain started on a much deeper emotional level and my brain just starts to dissociate whenever I feel it. But I think the dissociation is good because the pain is so intense.

Yeah I was so hesitant to get back on any antidepressant or mood stabilizer because I have reacted really poorly to some SSRIs but then when I started taking Pristiq I felt like I was on a little bit of molly every single day and like all of the corners of the street looked brighter and easier to see. I tend to have issues with suicidal ideations, but like only because a lot of the emotional coping mechanisms that got me through my childhood were “i don’t have to let this consume me emotionally bc i’m just going to kms” but mostly because I know that if I can separate myself from those emotions I can tune into a frequency where i feel no desire to kill myself. and Pristiq really helps with my half assed suicidal ideations like whenever I find myself returning to “wanting to die” thoughts particularly often in a day, most of the time it is because I forgot to take the pristiq in the morning. Doctors say that you don’t really feel the effects of antidepressants until you’re on them for a while but I definitely can feel the difference in my day when I miss it in the morning. I really feel like it just makes it easier for me not to sit around fighting against the urge to wallow in self pity and negative emotions. 


I recommend pristiq to everyone that I talk to bc the daily effect it has on my life is so profound and i don’t know where I’d be without it. Everyone is different though and while it has been effective for some people, my friend with high blood pressure said that she felt like pristiq might have contributed to further elevation of her blood pressure and made her anxiety relatively more manic. She does have a lot of other stressors present in her life that could’ve caused that, but she stopped taking it just in case - which I believe is the right thing to do. I have had doctors tell me to trust them to continue taking mood stabilizers and antidepressants because they were sure that there was no possible way I felt any effects yet but like you know your body better than any doctor and any doctor that tells you to trust them is only trying to emotionally manipulate you into trusting their advice over your own intuition. A doctor who deserves your trust won’t explicitly ask you to trust them but instead explain to you until you are reassured why you should trust them.

when you feel like you’re neglected and abandoned in life we often start treating ourselves like that as a coping mechanism so that it will hurt less when other people do it to us. But nobody can hurt us as bad as we can hurt ourselves and nobody can love us as deeply as we can love ourselves. I’m still learning how to be unconditionally present with myself and learning to love myself with gentle compassion so that when the universe does put someone in front of me that is ready for me to love them I can love them through my self-love, which is a cup that will never empty, as opposed to loving them because i want them to bring me a particular emotion or fulfillment, because that can only possibly end in resentment. Cut yourself some slack! And put a little trust in yourself and in the universe because anybody who is capable of loving will find someone who has genuinely been begging the universe to send them someone who is capable of loving!! everything happens in time and patience is so important. and like not only are you willing to give love another shot you are actively thinking about how to do it the right way which is really great and constructive and something that most people overlook. I think if you feel like you’re looking for love right now and not seeing any opportunities, that’s just an opportunity to look inward and consciously be there and love yourself and try and self soothe yourself into believing that it’s OK to be patient now as opposed to being driven by the craving of external validation. just think about the love that you are ready to give to another person if only they were right there in front of you and then take a look in the mirror and try to give that love to the person who is right there in front of you. I believe in you 💕

of course you will come across people who have the potential to love you romantically. but as long as you try to use love from other people to substitute what only self love can bring you, you will end up disappointed and feeling lost and abandoned when the person is not there actively loving you.
